priorities.finding: Prioritize a small, time-boxed follow-up on request-context features. Training-only screening shows a positive primary lift of 0.0022 across all four days, but the daily standard deviation exceeds the mean lift, so evidence is directional rather than strongly stable. The latest experiment has GAUC 0.6499 and primary 0.5885, with no measured parent gain available; do not scale budget without a controlled confirmation.
priorities.recommended_action: Run one confirmatory temporal holdout or ablation focused on tab, hour, and weekday interactions; stop further expansion if the lift is not reproduced.

priorities.finding: Post-score diagnostics show concentrated top-five weakness in tabs 8 and 5 and in rare items. These slices have very low nDCG@5 and primary, while rare items retain GAUC around 0.60, indicating that the main issue is top-five placement and coverage rather than uniformly poor within-user ordering.
priorities.recommended_action: Use targeted error analysis and limited reranking or exploration tests for these slices; do not infer broad model failure from the segment results.

avoid: Reject user-profile, historical user-author affinity, upload-recency, content-duration, item-metadata, historical-author-response, and historical-item-response additions because their training-only primary lifts are negative: screen:user_profile, screen:historical_user_author_affinity, screen:upload_recency, screen:content_duration, screen:item_metadata, screen:historical_author_response, screen:historical_item_response.
Do not use current-impression outcomes or aggregate snapshots without per-impression availability timestamps because they create leakage: experiment:1:metrics.
Do not treat user_positive_count:zero as a feature opportunity; it uses validation labels retrospectively and has GAUC 0.5 with zero top-five metrics: experiment:1:segment:user_positive_count:zero.
Do not allocate broad follow-on budget yet. The official validation diagnostics are slices rather than independent test estimates, and no observed parent gain is available: experiment:1:metrics.
metric_diagnosis: The model shows useful within-user ranking evidence overall, with GAUC 0.6499, but top-five quality is weaker in specific segments: global nDCG@5 is 0.5272 and primary is 0.5885, while tab 8 and tab 5 fall to primary 0.1282 and 0.1781. GAUC should be prioritized for assessing stable ordering; the rare-item slice illustrates that acceptable GAUC can coexist with weak top-five performance. Apply the strict early-stop rule: hold or stop broad experimentation after this run, and fund only a single leakage-safe confirmation of request-context gains plus targeted diagnostics for the identified weak segments.
